subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get their own `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue relying only on per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This choice defines a scheduled-run authorization boundary and a public config contract, and it can change existing cron message-delivery behavior.

options.title: Add cron-scoped tool policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence over global/provider/agent/sandbox/subagent policy and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus docs and tests.

options.title: Make cron inherit subagent policy
options.body: Reuse `tools.subagents.tools` for cron sessions, but document the coupling and add upgrade proof for existing cron jobs that currently rely on message delivery.

options.title: Keep per-job controls only
options.body: Decline a reusable cron config layer and document `payload.toolsAllow` as the supported hard policy surface for each job.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped tool policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence over global/provider/agent/sandbox/subagent policy and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus docs and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He already reviewed this issue as a cron tool-policy/product boundary and has strong adjacent cron/runtime history.
